newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Lonrho Uzbek gold project cost may rise.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho Uzbek gold project cost may rise.

text.p: The cost of an Uzbek gold project co-financed by British conglomerate Lonrho Plc and the International Finance Corporation will probably exceed its target of $355 million, an Uzbek official said on Friday.

The official, from the State Geology and Mineral Resources Committee, told Reuters that recent hikes in land taxes and electricity and water tariffs would affect the Amantaitau Goldfields project's budget.
The venture to develop Amantaitau is 57 percent owned by Uzbekistan, with 35 percent belonging to Lonrho and eight percent to the IFC, a unit of the World Bank.
Lonrho won a tender last year to take part in the project, in Uzbekistan's Navoi province.
The project consists of two stages involving the development of four open quarries, one underground mine and construction of an ore-enrichment facility to come on stream in the first quarter of 1998.
The source said construction had started in the second half of last year but that financing had not yet come through.
The field's reserves are equal to 300 tonnes of gold.
Trade journals say Uzbekistan is the world's ninth-largest gold producer, with output in 1996 of 60 tonnes.
